title: Base-flat complexes are tor-independent under pullback
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let g:T\to S be a morphism, let X be an S-scheme, and let g':X_T\to X be the projection [def-pc-base-change]. If G^\bullet is a bounded-above complex of quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-modules whose terms are flat over S, then for every x'\in X_T, with x=g'(x'), s the image of x in S, and t the image of x' in T, and every i\in\mathbf Z, the canonical stalkwise base-change map H^i(G_x^\bullet\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{T,t})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{T,t}}\mathcal O_{X_T,x'}\to H^i(((g')^*G^\bullet)_{x'}) is an isomorphism [def-pc-derived-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0A1D (lemma-base-change-tensor), proof: condition of Tag 0DJ8 checked on stalks

proof.text: Fix x' and write R=\mathcal O_{S,s}, A=\mathcal O_{X,x}, B=\mathcal O_{T,t}, and C=\mathcal O_{X_T,x'}. Each stalk G_x^n is a flat R-module: this is what the hypothesis that G^n is flat over S says at the point x (Stacks, Morphisms, Definition Tag 01U2); note it is flatness over S, not over X, that is used. Thus G_x^\bullet is a bounded-above complex of flat R-modules, and [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes it K-flat over R.

source.place: Tag 0A1D, proof of the stalkwise condition (using Tag 0DJ8 condition (1))

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the ring map R\to B on the one-point site (sheaves of modules are modules). Since G_x^\bullet is K-flat over R (Step 1), the identity is a K-flat resolution, so G_x^\bullet\otimes^L_R B is computed by the ordinary complex G_x^\bullet\otimes_R B; hence H^i(G_x^\bullet\otimes_R^L B)=H^i(G_x^\bullet\otimes_R B) canonically.

source.place: Tag 0A1D, proof of the stalkwise condition (using Tag 0DJ8 condition (1))

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] applied to g' and each term G^n, naturally in G^n and hence compatibly with the differentials, ((g')^*G^\bullet)_{x'}\cong G_x^\bullet\otimes_A C. The canonical map A\otimes_R B\to C is a localization (on affine opens Spec A_0, Spec B_0 over Spec R_0 the local ring C is a localization of A_0\otimes_{R_0}B_0, of which A\otimes_R B is itself a localization, by the affine description of fibre products, Stacks, Schemes, Section on fibre products), so C is flat over A\otimes_R B by exactness of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] and tensoring G_x^\bullet\otimes_R B with C commutes with taking H^i. Associativity of ordinary tensor products identifies (G_x^\bullet\otimes_R B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C with G_x^\bullet\otimes_A C. Under these identifications and Step 2 the displayed canonical map is the identity, so it is an isomorphism for every i.
